subject: History
description: 5 dynasties, key sultans, founders, falls + features

questions.stem: The DELHI SULTANATE consisted of FIVE successive dynasties. The FIRST one was:

options.option_text: Lodi dynasty, last of the five

questions.explanation: Delhi Sultanate (1206-1526 CE) = 5 dynasties: (1) MAMLUK / Slave (1206-1290) — Qutbuddin Aibak, Iltutmish, Razia Sultan (first + only female ruler), Balban; (2) KHALJI (1290-1320) — Jalaluddin, Alauddin Khalji (greatest); (3) TUGHLAQ (1320-1414) — Ghiyasuddin, Muhammad bin Tughlaq (eccentric experimenter), Firuz Shah; (4) SAYYID (1414-1451) — Khizr Khan founded after Timur's invasion; (5) LODI (1451-1526) — Bahlul, Sikandar, Ibrahim Lodi (defeated by Babur at PANIPAT 1526 → end of Sultanate, start of Mughals).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The QUTUB MINAR (Delhi) was started by:
questions.explanation: QUTUB MINAR — started by QUTBUDDIN AIBAK (1199; ground floor only) → completed by ILTUTMISH (his son-in-law + successor). Highest Indo-Islamic minaret (~73 m). Repaired by Firuz Shah Tughlaq (1368, after lightning damage) + Sikandar Lodi. ALAI MINAR (incomplete) was Alauddin Khalji's plan to build double the Qutub's height. UNESCO WHS (1993). Other adjacent monuments: Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Iron Pillar of Chandragupta Vikramaditya (rust-resistant! — 4th c. CE Gupta period), Tomb of Iltutmish.

questions.stem: RAZIA SULTAN was the only female ruler of the Sultanate. She belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: RAZIA SULTAN (r. 1236-1240) — daughter of ILTUTMISH; nominated by him as successor (preferring her over sons). FIRST + ONLY FEMALE RULER of Delhi Sultanate. Wore men's clothes; rode + ruled openly. Faced opposition from Turkish nobles + clergy. Allegedly fell for Yaqut (Abyssinian slave-officer she promoted) — caused outcry. Eventually deposed + killed (~1240) by hostile nobles + her brothers. Notable for early female leadership — preceded Razia by Hindu queens like Rudrama Devi (Kakatiya, ~1262-89).

questions.stem: ALAUDDIN KHALJI is famous for which administrative reform?

options.option_text: Banning Persian as a court language

questions.explanation: ALAUDDIN KHALJI (r. 1296-1316) — possibly the most ambitious + ruthless Delhi Sultan. Innovations: (1) MARKET REFORMS — fixed prices for grain, cloth, slaves, animals, etc. in Delhi; created markets for each commodity (Mandi); spies (DIWAN-I-RIYASAT) ensured compliance — to support large army cheaply. (2) Land revenue measured by area + yield (1/2 of produce as tax). (3) Built army of horsemen, paid in cash (not jagirs). (4) Stopped expansion of Mongol invasions (3 invasions failed). (5) Conquests in south (deccan campaigns by Malik Kafur — looted Yadavas, Hoysalas, Pandyas). Built ALAI DARWAZA (Qutub complex), Siri Fort. Distractor 3: jizya was reduced/abolished by Akbar much later.

questions.stem: MUHAMMAD BIN TUGHLAQ is famous for which infamous decision?

options.option_text: Building the Taj Mahal in Agra
Capital shift Delhi to Daulatabad and back
Abolition of all forms of taxation

questions.explanation: MUHAMMAD BIN TUGHLAQ (r. 1325-1351) — eccentric ambitious sultan. Known for 5 'experiments' (mostly failures!): (1) Shifted CAPITAL from Delhi to DAULATABAD / Devagiri (1327; meant for better control of Deccan; forced entire population to march south — many died; abandoned + reverted to Delhi 1335). (2) TOKEN CURRENCY — copper / brass coins valued same as silver (1330; rampant counterfeiting → currency collapse). (3) TAXATION in Doab — sharply raised; then drought hit; revolts. (4) Plan to invade Khurasan (Persia) — never executed. (5) Plan to conquer Karachil (Tibet area) — disaster, army wiped out. Had vast learning + ambition but lacked judgement. Ibn Battuta visited his court.

questions.stem: TIMUR (Tamerlane) of Central Asia INVADED + sacked Delhi in:
questions.explanation: TIMUR (Tamerlane; founder of Timurid Empire) invaded India 1398 — sacked DELHI under last Tughlaq sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud. Sacked Delhi (massacred + plundered for days), took skilled craftsmen, jewels, women back to Samarkand. Caused near-collapse of Tughlaq dynasty. Left Khizr Khan as governor — Khizr later founded SAYYID dynasty (1414). Timur was great-great-great grandfather of BABUR (Mughal founder, descended via Timur on father's side + Genghis on mother's). Distractor 1 = Muhammad Ghori vs Prithviraj Chauhan. Distractor 3 = founding of Mughals. Distractor 4 = Marathas vs Abdali.

questions.stem: The DELHI SULTANATE ended with the FIRST BATTLE OF PANIPAT in 1526. The defeated sultan was:

options.option_text: Ibrahim Lodi, last sultan of the era
Sher Shah Suri, who came later

questions.explanation: FIRST BATTLE OF PANIPAT (21 April 1526) — Babur (Mughal Timurid prince, with ~12,000 men + early CANNONS, MUSKETS, formation tactics — TULUGHMA) defeated IBRAHIM LODI (~100,000 troops + war elephants; out-of-date tactics). Ibrahim Lodi killed in battle → end of Delhi Sultanate, start of MUGHAL EMPIRE. Babur went on to win SECOND major battle KHANWA 1527 (vs Rana Sanga) + Ghaghra (vs Afghans). Distractor 1: Sikandar Lodi died 1517. Distractor 3: Bahlul founded dynasty 1451. Distractor 4: Sher Shah Suri later defeated Humayun (1540) → set up Suri dynasty (1540-1555).
